body:
Closing this — **the report is wrong, and there is no bug here.** My instrumentation was
measuring a file that never executes.

## What actually happens

For a **directory-source** marketplace, `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` resolves to the plugin
directory **inside the source working tree**, not to the versioned dir under
`~/.claude/plugins/cache/`. The cache dir is populated on install, but the hook command runs
against the live source tree.

I had put the canary shim in the cache dir. Under a github source that *is* the executed
path, so the canary fired. Under a directory source the executed path is the repo, so the
cache-dir copy I was watching sat untouched — and I read that silence as "hooks don't run".

## How it was caught

The session itself contradicted me. With `policy.json` present, the model quoted the injected
`[cli-dispatch policy] …` block back verbatim while my canary file was still absent. Text
cannot reach the context without the hook producing it, so the hook was plainly running and my
probe was in the wrong place.

Placing an identical shim in the source tree instead settles it, same session, same install:

```
REPO-path hook:  FIRED
CACHE-path hook: ABSENT
```

## Corrected result

| marketplace source | `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` | hook runs |
|---|---|---|
| github | versioned cache dir | yes |
| directory | source working tree | yes |

Directory-source hooks work, and running them from the working tree is the useful behavior for
plugin development — an edit takes effect in the next session with no reinstall.

Apologies for the noise. Everything under "What I ruled out" in the original report still holds
(print vs interactive, trust, version, interpreter, `SessionStart` delivery) — those eliminations
were sound; the conclusion drawn from them was not.
